subject.title: Add an FxTwitter read transport for public lookups, threads, profiles, and search

question: Should Birdclaw core accept and support an explicitly selected public FxTwitter endpoint, including its privacy, endpoint-trust, reliability, and capability contract?
rationale: The architecture can accommodate this transport, but code inspection cannot decide whether the project should assume ongoing responsibility for a third-party public service and configurable endpoint.

options.title: Approve scoped core transport
options.body: Allow an explicit-only FxTwitter adapter with strict capability boundaries, safe endpoint validation, attribution, bounded retries, and no implicit fallback.

options.title: Require self-hosting only
options.body: Permit the adapter only for explicitly configured self-hosted FxEmbed deployments, avoiding endorsement of the shared public endpoint.

options.title: Keep it outside core
options.body: Retain bird and xurl as the core transports and leave FxTwitter integration to an external consumer or future extension surface.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped core transport
recommendation.body: Allow an explicit-only FxTwitter adapter with strict capability boundaries, safe endpoint validation, attribution, bounded retries, and no implicit fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository specification identifies this person as project owner, and the unresolved choice is a core product and privacy boundary.
